source.publisher: Engineer-in-Chief's Branch, General Headquarters, Rawalpindi (Ministry of Defence, Military Engineer Services, Pakistan)
source.edition: MES Schedule of Rates - 2014 (First Edition, August 2014)
source.notes: MES Schedule of Rates 2014 (First Edition, August 2014), compiled under the orders of the Engineer-in-Chief, GHQ Rawalpindi; foreword dated September 2014. It replaced MES SR 2009 (reprints 2010/2012/2013). Source: the complete 736-page PDF that was published as an attachment to a UNDP Pakistan procurement notice. Text was extracted with pdfplumber; the red 'MILITARY ENGINEER SERVICES' watermark was filtered out, and items were read from the 'Sl No | Description | Unit | Rate (Rs)' tables in sections 1-29 and the 'Labour Rates' table in section 31. Section 30 (cement consumption sheet, which has no rates) is excluded. There are 6588 rated items: sections 1-27 are composite work items (kind=item), sections 28-29 are 'Material Supply Only' rates (kind=material) and section 31 gives daily labour rates (kind=labour, unit=day). Every rate was cross-checked against a second, independent layout-text extraction of the same page (0 mismatches), and 20 random rows were checked by hand against the raw PDF text (20/20 match). Left out: 81 items printed with no rate (marked '(Deleted being obsolete)' or 'Deleted being shifted to section 27'), plus 28-149 and 29-538, which have no rate printed in the source. Two rows printed without an item number were also skipped: one after 29-388 ('Same as item 29-387 but 225 lit.', Rs 27,033) and one after 29-551 (Rs 7,502,000). Two misprinted codes were corrected from the surrounding numbering: '2-5' printed on the Pre-Engineered Construction page became 22-5, and a second '29-62' between 29-621 and 29-623 became 29-622. 29-612 is kept as printed (Rs 1,336,125.65), although its neighbours suggest a misprint of about Rs 133,612. Unit normalisation: Cum->m3, Sqm->m2, Metre->m, Kg->kg, Tonne/Ton->t (metric tonne), Lit->l. Each/Point/Set/Pair/Per set->pcs, with the rate unchanged, so one pcs is one point, set or pair as printed. 'C.No' and 'C Rifles' are per hundred (rate/100). 'M.Nos' is per thousand (rate/1000). Dozen is rate/12. '90 M coil' cables are rate/90 per m. Cement 'Bag' is divided by the bag weight stated in the description (40 or 50 kg). Three section-28 items printed without a unit were set to pcs. Codes are kept exactly as printed (the book cites them zero-padded in its text, e.g. 'item 01-6') and are sorted numerically by section and item. GST is included in the rates (General Rule 25). IMPORTANT: MES SR 2014 is not the current edition. Current MES tenders quote against 'MES Schedule of Rates 2021, amended up to date, including the Ruling Percentage issued by MES'. The 2021 edition and its amendments and ruling-percentage letters are sold by E-in-C's Branch and are not publicly downloadable; only login-gated Scribd uploads were found, and they were not used. 2014 rates are therefore below 2026 market levels. Apply the contract or tender premium and an escalation allowance; see SOURCES.md.
